Liddle syndrome is a genetic disorder inherited in an autosomal dominant manner that is characterized by early, and frequently severe, high blood pressure associated with low plasma renin activity, metabolic alkalosis, low blood potassium, and normal to low levels of aldosterone.
  • Non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia occurs due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency (NCAH) is a milder and later onset form of a genetic condition known as congenital adrenal hyperplasia.  Affected people generally experience symptoms of androgen excess such as acne, premature development of pubic hair, reduced adult height, etc. Women with NCAH are generally born with normal female genitalia. Later in life, signs and symptoms of the condition can vary but may include hirsutism, frontal baldness, delayed menarche, infertility.
  • Bartter syndrome (BS) is a hereditary condition transmitted as an autosomal recessive (Bartter type 1 to 4) or dominant trait (Bartter type 5). The disease is associated with hypokalemic alkalosis and varying degree of hypercalciuria and normal to low blood pressures.
  • Diabetic nephropathy is a clinical syndrome characterized by persistent albuminuria (>300 mg/d or >200 μg/min) that is confirmed on at least 2 occasions 3–6 months apart, progressive decline in the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and elevated arterial blood pressure. It is a complication of diabetes mellitus. Over many years, the condition slowly damages the kidney’s delicate filtering system and progresses into kidney failure also called ESRD.

• Stress hormones are secreted in response to stressful or exciting situations. Long-term stress is associated with high levels of cortisol. These are steroid hormones secreted by the adrenal cortex which has a marked effect on carbohydrate metabolism and acts as an immunosuppressant.

• Class C category of fire extinguisher is preferred if an MRI machine catches electric fire because this category deals with fire related to electric equipment.  A class C fire is an energized electrical fire.   • A class C fire requires an agent that can break apart the elements that feed a fire: oxygen, heat, and fuel. Carbon dioxide (CO2) extinguishers smother a fire by eliminating the oxygen. They also suppress the fire’s heat because their discharge is very cold. Similarly, dry chemical extinguishers work to separate the elements of a fire.
  • The fire dies when the oxygen and fuel can no longer interact due to the chemicals introduced by a dry chemical extinguisher.  These Class C fire extinguishers may contain monoammonium phosphate, potassium bicarbonate, or potassium chloride, all of which are suitable for putting out class C fires.
